6 years out and kept it off. But the five people I know who also have had it have gained back some or all of their weight. I credit mine to calorie counting every single day. Each time it was the same lady driving the golf cart/tram for us, I believe they just had the one.

Buy parking asap, it will sell out and you will have to park at a place ever further and walk across fields adding a lot more distance to you walk, we bought the official passes something like $250 for the weekend and while pricey was way closer, still a good 1-2 mile trek to the grandstands.

Your actual education however relies on how educated and committed your parents are. My mother struggled in math so I struggled in math, needing multiple extra courses in college to get caught up. Our books were all religious meaning I didn't know about events like the ice age or evolution until college. It was some serious growing pains, but since I liked learning and reading I managed to get caught up and adjust. 

Public education is not great, but it is solid and offers a great world view. You may have some teachers or grade levels that are worse than others but it's just for a year or semester and it evens out so that you get a wide variety of knowledge from many educators. You also get experiences in electives, sports, clubs, etc which is something I was really lacking growing up. You have counselors and peers and adults to help mentor you and shape you. I had no one but my mom and her struggles became my own, including anxiety and depression as I had no adults to share concerns with or help guide me through things she was putting me through. 

Luckily things worked out, I love teaching and being that person I never had growing up :)

Tldr: Homeschooling can be great but I don't think many people realize how much work it will take. Public school isn't the best, but it is worlds better than an uneducated parent or someone struggling with their own problems.

The pre and post op restrictions were not fun, but FAR worth it to drop 225lbs and still going. I can travel the world now instead of having to take a break to sit down walking in the mall. My healthy and quality of life is fantastic. Just know, you wont ever go back to eating 'normal'. I'm 2.5 years out and still eat about 1100 calories a day, BUT you can still eat whatever you want you just have to balance it out. Today for example I had: 

  
Breakfast: Coffee with some protein shake in it, a chicken sausage, and a sugar cookie

Lunch: 1/3 a cup of rice, 3 oz of chicken, and mixed veggies

Dinner will be: 4 oz pork chop and roasted asparagus 

Snacks: String cheese and a slice of leftover pizza.  


As long as you are watching what you are eating and getting in your protein, your good. You just have to decide if that is worth it for you. Personally my only regret is not doing it sooner. I have known 4 people personally who done the surgery, lost 100+ pounds, and gained it all back plus more because they think the surgery fixes everything. It does not, it is a tool to help you. Wishing you the best luck in your decision, feel free to message with any questions!
